newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions set Sept 26-27 for general strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions set Sept 26-27 for general strike.

text.p: Argentina's labor federation CGT Thursday set Sept 26-27 as the date for its 36-hour general strike and said the walkout will include a demonstration in front of the Casa Rosada government house.
CGT secretary general Gerardo Martinez, at a union meeting held Thursday at a soccer stadium in Buenos Aires, said the strike is in protest of government economic austerity plans.
"The strike will be a smashing success because we will have the people on our side," said Martinez after union leaders voted in favor of the walkout.
Earlier in the day, Martinez called for the unity of the labor movement to better confront the economic reforms.
"There is no economic recovery and growth. There is more poverty. That is why we need the unity of the labor movement," he said.

The labor movement has shown profound divisions in past years. The CGT, the largest union group, had sided with President Carlos Menem's economic reforms while many unions rallied around two splinter labor groups, the CTA and the MTA.
With 17.1 percent unemployment, the entire labor movement held a successfull general strike August 8 to protest belt-tightening measures launched by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.

After his successor, Roque Fernandez, confirmed he would continue with the reforms and announced his own set of austerity measures, the unions said they would continue their "fight" with another walkout.
